memory_update.text: For specialized AI cloud capacity, CRWV and NBIS should be treated as reference leaders rather than underfollowed alpha candidates because public attention and large customer announcements are already high.

IREN remains relevant to the underfollowed lane because the market may still classify it through a bitcoin-mining lens, but the AI-cloud thesis requires verification of contracted revenue, financing terms, power economics, and utilization.

APLD is a second-order AI capacity candidate focused on powered data-center campuses and leasing rather than pure GPU-cloud software; it should be evaluated on power, construction execution, lease terms, counterparty quality, and balance-sheet survivability.

The key chokepoint variables for this node are not GPU ownership alone; survival through Layer 2 requires evidence of connected power, customer contracts, financing durability, deployment speed, depreciation assumptions, and realized utilization.

The current U.S.-listed universe of pure-play AI-cloud capacity names is small and increasingly well followed; further underfollowed discovery may need to move one step sideways into data-center developers, power equipment, liquid cooling, interconnect, leasing finance, and AI infrastructure software orchestration.

summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for specialized AI cloud capacity and GPU-as-a-service infrastructure. The cleanest reference names are CoreWeave and Nebius because they operate AI-cloud capacity directly and have disclosed or reported large customer relationships with AI labs, hyperscalers, or Meta. The underfollowed/discovery lane is narrower because several names have already rerated, but IREN and Applied Digital remain relevant as power-backed AI data-center or GPU-cloud capacity plays with execution, financing, lease, utilization, and customer-concentration risks.
